newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Armed Forces of the Philippines says the Chinese are building new structures on disputed shoals in the Spratly islands (MANILA TIMES)

- World powers flying in to Hong Kong for the handover warn Beijing to keep its promises on the territory's future even as the the new government announces that first elections under Chinese rules will take place in May. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Kidnap-for-ransom groups snatch three Filipino-Chinese businessmen in separate incidents over the weekend in Manila. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Cabinet members who signed a petition to amend the Constitution to extend the term of President Ramos face possible Senate sanction, united opposition leaders warn (TODAY)
- San Miguel Corp is cutting its beer prices by 14 percent starting today. (MANILA TIMES)
- Energy Secretary Francisco Viray says he is open to possible changes in the Oil Deregulation Law being proposed by the Senate. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The International Monetary Fund has rejected the Philippine government's bid to reduce its revenue programme by 23.2 billion pesos to 460.2 billion. (TODAY)
- Exxon Co Inc plans to stage a comeback in the Philippines where it will invest in a new oil refinery and fuel distribution facilities. (MANILA BULLETIN)
